structured.approach: Attempt 2 fixes the G1 refusal. The SS-1 row said that "this lane never reads source-system production data", and neither cited source states that general rule. I removed the sentence. SS-1 now says only what feat.tasks supports: feed v3 in production (PQ-6) gates the release of TSK-01, not its coding, and coding builds on synthetic v3 rows. The re-entry handling is quoted from the brief's trigger ("Task creation, or any re-entry trigger"). I then checked every other statement the same way. I rewrote SS-2 because it named later lane steps (DE-13, DE-14) and email/Teams notifications that no cited source supports. It now says only that no input names a secret for any later step, citing tool:repo-access and the brief's trigger. I also replaced the "Production data read: None" validation row with the items this step actually read. The rest is unchanged. I re-checked the two Data Engineering tasks (TSK-01, TSK-02) in feat.tasks, which I fetched with context_get in attempt 1 for a receipt. I used the approved DE-01 output task.repo_access as background. The permission table's verdict comes from the tool view, because org.permission_table is restricted and passed by reference only. The outcome is that no secret is required, none is granted, there is no gap and no access request is raised. I rewrote the output file in full and kept the tool-result line the spine had appended.
tools_used: Grep (ap_pipeline checkout, secret-reference cross-check; not cited)

claims.text: No secrets are required or granted for the ap_pipeline repository, according to the permission table as reported by the tool view.
The Data Engineering lane's tasks in scope are TSK-01 (optional paid_date in to_model) and TSK-02 (delays_by_vendor), both on the ap_pipeline repository.
TSK-01 must not change ingest.py, dq.py, pipeline.py or schedule.json, and coding builds on synthetic v3 rows, so it needs no feed credential.
TSK-02 is a new pure function with no I/O that does not change its input records, so it needs no secret.
The tasks use only the Python 3.9 standard library and choose no new technology.
Feed v3 in production (PQ-6) gates the release of TSK-01, not its coding.
Databricks is not applicable to ap_pipeline, and DE-01 found no workspace credential to check.
Work runs on branch feature/story, and CI is run with /usr/bin/python3 ci.py.
DE-02 is triggered by task creation or any re-entry trigger, so a secret needed later re-enters this step.
org.permission_table is restricted and passed by reference only; this output does not open or quote it.

open_questions: Non-blocking (SS-1): if releasing TSK-01 against the production v3 feed (PQ-6) needs a feed credential, DE-02 should run again on that re-entry trigger. Proposed owner: Data engineering lead.
Non-blocking (SS-2): no input names a secret for any later step of this lane. If one needs a secret, DE-02 should run again on that re-entry trigger. Proposed owner: Data engineering lead.
structured.summary: I rewrote task.secrets_scope.md for DE-02, attempt 2. I removed the unsupported general statement about production data from SS-1 and narrowed SS-2 and the validation row to what the sources state. The finding has not changed: TSK-01 and TSK-02 on ap_pipeline need no secrets, and the permission table, as the tool view reports it, grants none. That holds for local/CI and for the dev and main branches, so there is no gap and no access request. The restricted permission table was handled by reference only, and no secret values appear. There are no blocking questions.
